subject: Private VPC & control plane — clarifying networking, air-gap feasibility, and next tests
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@finserv.com>
Cc: Anika Patel <anika@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC & control plane — clarifying networking, air-gap feasibility, and next tests

Rajiv / Anika — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we’re aligned: 

Summary from our call:
- FinServ is evaluating private deployments for latency, data residency, and auditability.
- You asked for a clear comparison vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints and a way to validate an air-gapped/on-prem option.
- Key concerns: control plane placement, HSM/KMS integration, outbound networking restrictions, and SOC2 evidence.

What Redwood can demonstrate (short list):
- Private control plane (customer-managed or split-mode) with optional VPC peering so control signals do not traverse public internet.
- Data plane entirely inside customer VPC with private ENIs; KV cache and model artifacts served from a mirrored registry inside your network for air-gapped installs.
- KMS/HSM integrations via PKCS#11 bridge or cloud KMS, plus audit log exports and optional retention policies.

Proposed next tests (we’ll run these in your dev VPC):
1) Network connectivity smoke test: verify VPC peering / AWS Transit / Private IP routing for inference traffic (we’ll validate NAT/firewall rules).
2) Control plane mode validation: 1) Redwood-managed control plane with private tunnels, 2) Customer-managed private control plane in your VPC (we’ll deploy a single-node control plane).
3) Air-gap feasibility: show a workflow to seed model artifacts and image registry, then perform an offline restart with no outbound access.
4) Security checklist items: HSM/KMS test (rotate a key), log ingest (to your SIEM), and show audit log exports.

Attachments: redwood-rfi-checklist.xlsx, networking-diagram.pdf — I’ve included a concise checklist and a simple diagram of the two deployment patterns we discussed.

Asks from your side:
- Can you confirm a sandbox AWS account (or a dev VPC) we can use for the tests and a point-of-contact for networking (Anika?)
- Please share any minimum compliance artifacts you need up front (e.g., SOC2 cert, the specific security questionnaire file).
- Preferred window for a 2–3 hour smoke test next week.

I’ll loop in engineering (Rishi) to scope the control-plane tests and time estimates after you confirm the sandbox and window.

– Evelyn
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: Private VPC & control plane — clarifying networking, air-gap feasibility, and next tests

Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

- HSM/KMS: we run keys in an HSM (Thales) and require either on-host PKCS#11 or an approved KMS proxy. Can Redwood connect to our HSM via a customer-managed gateway?
- Control plane ownership: does "customer-managed" mean you ship a containerized control plane that we run, or does Redwood still have an operator that needs outbound access for upgrade/monitoring?
- Air-gap: what is the proposed mechanism for artifact mirroring and software updates when there is zero outbound access? Any offline install playbook you can share?

We can provide a dev AWS account (arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/Redwood-PoC) with a VPC and a designated networking lead (Anika will own).

We also have a security questionnaire and will attach it once I review the checklist you sent. Preferred test window: Dec 2–3 (US PST mornings).

– Rajiv
Rajiv Sharma
Head of Platform Engineering, FinServ Capital
rajiv@finserv.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Private VPC & control plane — clarifying networking, air-gap feasibility, and next tests

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 15:01 Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@finserv.com> wrote:
> Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 
> 
> - HSM/KMS: we run keys in an HSM (Thales) and require either on-host PKCS#11 or an approved KMS proxy. Can Redwood connect to our HSM via a customer-managed gateway?
> - Control plane ownership: does "customer-managed" mean you ship a containerized control plane that we run, or does Redwood still have an operator that needs outbound access for upgrade/monitoring?
> - Air-gap: what is the proposed mechanism for artifact mirroring and software updates when there is zero outbound access? Any offline install playbook you can share?

Rajiv — quick technical answers and proposed approaches: 

1) HSM/KMS: yes. We support PKCS#11-compatible HSMs and can operate against an on-prem gateway. For cloud HSMs we also support key wrapping with your KMS and can integrate our signing/secret retrieval via a proxy you control. We will need a short window to validate PKCS#11 bindings during the PoC.

2) Control plane modes (two supported models):
  a) Split/semi-managed: Redwood runs the control plane as a managed service, but you can limit control-plane egress to specific IPs with a private relay/tunnel (no public endpoints exposed to the internet). This mode allows Redwood to push upgrades and maintain health checks.
  b) Customer-managed: we provide the control plane as a containerized deployment (K8s Helm chart / operator-less binary) that you run inside your VPC. No Redwood operator access required. For upgrades you can either accept signed upgrade bundles or we can provide an offline bundle and a step-by-step apply.

3) Air-gap / artifact mirroring: our offline flow is twofold: 1) mirror images and model artifacts into an internal registry (we provide a sync tool with checksum verification), 2) provide signed release artifact bundles and a verified install script (no outbound required). The private-controlplane-playbook.md (attached) has the exact steps we follow for an air-gapped install.

Smoke-test plan (detailed):
- Day 0: Confirm IAM role + VPC peering details and open a short list of firewall rules we’ll need.
- Day 1: Deploy a single-node private control plane into your dev VPC, run a connectivity test (TLS handshake, L4 pass).
- Day 1 afternoon: Deploy a small model (e.g., t5-small equivalent) from mirrored registry and run inference workflow; capture latency and token throughput.
- Day 2: Run HSM key rotation demo and validate audit logs and export pipeline to your SIEM.

We’ll be able to run the initial smoke tests in a half-day for the connectivity/control-plane checks and ~2–3 hours for model deployment and verification. I’ll drive the runbook and will bring the playbook and tooling.

Attachments: private-controlplane-playbook.md (I’ve attached the doc that Rajiv asked for).

If this plan looks good to you (Rajiv), we can lock Dec 2 morning (PST).

– Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
